obligations.summary: The Commission must without undue delay enter into consultation with the relevant market surveillance authority and the operator(s) and evaluate the national measure when objections are raised or the measure is considered contrary to Union law.
exceptions: Standard objection window is three months from notification under Article 79(5); reduced to 30 days for non-compliance with prohibited AI practices under Article 5.

obligations.summary: The Commission must issue a decision within six months (or 60 days for Article 5 prohibited practices) from the notification under Article 79(5) on whether the national measure is justified, and notify all market surveillance authorities of its decision.
exceptions: Deadline is reduced to 60 days when non-compliance concerns prohibited AI practices under Article 5.

obligations.summary: Where the Commission considers the national measure justified, all Member States must take appropriate restrictive measures in respect of the AI system concerned, such as requiring its withdrawal from their market without undue delay, and inform the Commission accordingly.
Where the Commission considers the national measure unjustified, the Member State concerned must withdraw the measure and inform the Commission accordingly.

Where the national measure is justified and non-compliance is attributed to shortcomings in harmonised standards or common specifications, the Commission must apply the procedure provided for in Article 11 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012.
